sn46.16:1.1.pli: Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
sn46.16:1.1.eng: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn46.16:1.2.pli: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
sn46.16:1.2.eng: Now at that time he was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

sn46.16:1.3.pli: Atha kho āyasmā mahācundo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ mahācundaṃ bhagavā etadavoca:
sn46.16:1.3.eng: Then Venerable Mahācunda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

sn46.16:1.4.eng: “Cunda, express your understanding of the awakening factors.”

sn46.16:2.1.pli: “Sattime, bhante, bojjhaṅgā bhagavatā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti.
sn46.16:2.1.eng: “Sir, the Buddha has rightly explained these seven awakening factors. When developed and cultivated, they lead to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to extinguishment.

sn46.16:2.3.pli: Satisambojjhaṅgo kho, bhante, bhagavatā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo kho, bhante, bhagavatā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.
sn46.16:2.3.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.16:2.4.pli: Ime kho, bhante, satta bojjhaṅgā bhagavatā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattantī”ti.
sn46.16:2.4.eng: These are the seven awakening factors that the Buddha has rightly explained. When developed and cultivated, they lead to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to extinguishment.”

sn46.16:2.6.eng: Indeed, Cunda, these are awakening factors!”

sn46.16:3.3.eng: And that’s how the Buddha recovered from that illness.

sn46.16:3.4.pli: Tathāpahīno ca bhagavato so ābādho ahosīti.

sn46.17:1.1.pli: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattanti.
sn46.17:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, when these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.

sn46.17:1.3.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.17:1.4.pli: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattantīti.
sn46.17:1.4.eng: These seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.

sn46.17:2.2.eng: who cross to the far shore.

sn46.17:3.1.eng: When the teaching is well explained,

sn46.17:3.3.eng: are the ones who will cross over

sn46.17:3.4.eng: Death’s dominion so hard to pass.

sn46.17:4.2.eng: an astute person should develop the bright.

sn46.17:4.4.eng: for the seclusion so hard to enjoy,

sn46.17:5.4.eng: should cleanse themselves of mental corruptions.

sn46.17:6.1.eng: And those whose minds are rightly developed

sn46.17:6.6.eng: they are quenched in this world.”

sn46.175-184:3.1.eng: (Tell in full as in the chapter on removal of greed, hate, and delusion.)

sn46.175-184:3.2.eng: (The Linked Discourses on Awakening Factors should be told in full just as the Linked Discourses on the Path.)

sn46.175-184:3.3.eng: The Linked Discourses on the Awakening Factors is the second section.

sn46.18:1.1.pli: “Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā viraddhā, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī.
sn46.18:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, whoever has missed out on the seven awakening factors has missed out on the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn46.18:1.2.pli: Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā āraddhā, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī.
sn46.18:1.2.eng: Whoever has undertaken the seven awakening factors has undertaken the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn46.18:1.4.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.18:1.5.pli: yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ime satta bojjhaṅgā viraddhā, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī.
sn46.18:1.5.eng: Whoever has missed out on these seven awakening factors has missed out on the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn46.18:1.6.pli: Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ime satta bojjhaṅgā āraddhā, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī”ti.
sn46.18:1.6.eng: Whoever has undertaken these seven awakening factors has undertaken the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.”

sn46.19:1.1.pli: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ariyā niyyānikā nīyanti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
sn46.19:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, when these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they are noble and emancipating, and bring one who practices them to the complete ending of suffering.

sn46.19:1.3.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.19:1.4.pli: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ariyā niyyānikā nīyanti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā”ti.
sn46.19:1.4.eng: When these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they are noble and emancipating, and bring one who practices them to the complete ending of suffering.”

sn46.2:1.2.pli: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati;
sn46.2:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, this body is sustained by food. It depends on food to continue, and without food it doesn’t continue.
sn46.2:1.2.comm: For the phrase “sustained by food” see DN 33:1.8.2, AN 10.27:10.5, AN 10.28:4.5, Kp 4:1.2 and notes. The word āhāra, literally “intake”, may be translated as “food” or “fuel” depending on context.

sn46.2:1.3.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.
sn46.2:1.3.eng: In the same way, the five hindrances are sustained by fuel. They depend on fuel to continue, and without fuel they don’t continue.
sn46.2:1.3.comm: This passage can be seen as an expansion of the fourth satipaṭṭhāna, “observation of principles”, where the “principles” underlying the rise and fall of the hindrances and awakening factors are investigated. Similar teachings recur throughout this section, for example SN 46.51.

sn46.2:2.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya?
sn46.2:2.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow?

sn46.2:2.2.eng: There is the feature of beauty.
sn46.2:2.2.comm: “Feature of beauty” is subhanimitta. In early Pali, nimitta is used for a feature or quality of the mind that, when focused on, promotes the growth of similar or related qualities. Thus focusing on beauty fosters the desire for that beauty. (See MN 5:6.1).

sn46.2:2.3.eng: Frequent irrational application of mind to that
sn46.2:2.3.comm: “Irrational” attention sees the beauty as something to be held on to and appropriated. The flaw lies not in the object, but in the response.

sn46.2:2.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.
sn46.2:2.4.eng: fuels the arising of sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow.

sn46.2:3.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya?
sn46.2:3.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of ill will, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow?

sn46.2:3.2.eng: There is the feature of aversion.

sn46.2:3.3.eng: Frequent irrational application of mind to that

sn46.2:3.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.
sn46.2:3.4.eng: fuels the arising of ill will, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow.

sn46.2:4.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya?
sn46.2:4.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow?

sn46.2:4.2.pli: Atthi, bhikkhave, arati tandi vijambhitā bhattasammado cetaso ca līnattaṃ.
sn46.2:4.2.eng: There is discontent, sloth, yawning, sleepiness after eating, and mental sluggishness.

sn46.2:4.3.eng: Frequent irrational application of mind to them

sn46.2:4.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.
sn46.2:4.4.eng: fuels the arising of dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow.

sn46.2:5.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya?
sn46.2:5.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of restlessness and remorse, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow?

sn46.2:5.2.comm: Worrying about anxiety makes the mind even more anxious.

sn46.2:5.3.eng: Frequent irrational application of mind to that

sn46.2:5.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.
sn46.2:5.4.eng: fuels the arising of restlessness and remorse, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow.

sn46.2:6.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya?
sn46.2:6.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of doubt, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow?

sn46.2:6.2.eng: There are things that are grounds for doubt.
sn46.2:6.2.comm: Such as what the nature of the correct path (AN 3.65:3.8), the various wrong views (SN 24.1:5.1), the status of a saint after death (SN 44.9:5.2), or the reality of kamma (SN 42.13:21.2).

sn46.2:6.3.eng: Frequent irrational application of mind to them

sn46.2:6.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.
sn46.2:6.4.eng: fuels the arising of doubt, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow.

sn46.2:7.1.pli: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati;
sn46.2:7.1.eng: This body is sustained by food. It depends on food to continue, and without food it doesn’t continue.

sn46.2:7.2.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, ime pañca nīvaraṇā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.
sn46.2:7.2.eng: In the same way, the five hindrances are sustained by fuel. They depend on fuel to continue, and without fuel they don’t continue.

sn46.2:8.1.pli: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati;
sn46.2:8.1.eng: This body is sustained by food. It depends on food to continue, and without food it doesn’t continue.

sn46.2:8.2.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.
sn46.2:8.2.eng: In the same way, the seven awakening factors are sustained by fuel. They depend on fuel to continue, and without fuel they don’t continue.

sn46.2:9.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā?
sn46.2:9.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of mindfulness, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.2:9.2.eng: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of mindfulness.
sn46.2:9.2.comm: These include the meditations listed in the Satipaṭṭhana Sutta (MN 10).

sn46.2:9.3.eng: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.2:9.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.
sn46.2:9.4.eng: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of mindfulness, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.2:10.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā?
sn46.2:10.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of investigation of principles, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.2:10.2.pli: Atthi, bhikkhave, kusalākusalā dhammā, sāvajjānavajjā dhammā, hīnapaṇītā dhammā, kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā.
sn46.2:10.2.eng: There are qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and those with a portion of dark or bright.
sn46.2:10.2.comm: Discrimination between good and evil is the foundation of wisdom. | The phrase sappaṭibhāgā, which appears here in a stock phrase, is given three mutually exclusive explanations in the commentary (see Bodhi’s note on this sutta). I think the commentary is influenced by the later sense of paṭibhāgā as a technical meditation term meaning “counterpart”. This sense is, however, absent from Sanskrit, where pratibhāga means “portion, share” (Rig Veda 8.99.3, Manu 8.307). The sense would then refer to individuals “with a portion” of dark or bright qualities. This is, in fact, the theme of the only other passage in Pali that uses this term (AN 6.62:10.2).

sn46.2:10.3.eng: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.2:10.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.
sn46.2:10.4.eng: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of investigation of principles, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.2:11.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā?
sn46.2:11.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of energy, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.2:11.2.eng: There are the elements of initiative, persistence, and exertion.

sn46.2:11.3.eng: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.2:11.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.
sn46.2:11.4.eng: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of energy, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.2:12.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā?
sn46.2:12.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of rapture, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.2:12.2.eng: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of rapture.
sn46.2:12.2.comm: These are the things that bring wholesome joy to the mind, in and out of meditation.

sn46.2:12.3.eng: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.2:12.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.
sn46.2:12.4.eng: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of rapture, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.2:13.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā?
sn46.2:13.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of tranquility, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.2:13.2.eng: There is tranquility of the body and of the mind.

sn46.2:13.3.eng: Frequent rational application of mind to that

sn46.2:13.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.
sn46.2:13.4.eng: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of tranquility, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.2:14.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā?
sn46.2:14.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of immersion, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.2:14.2.eng: There are things that are the basis of serenity and freedom from distraction.
sn46.2:14.2.comm: The includes peaceful meditations such as mindfulness of breathing.

sn46.2:14.3.eng: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.2:14.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.
sn46.2:14.4.eng: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of immersion, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.2:15.1.pli: Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā?
sn46.2:15.1.eng: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of equanimity, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.2:15.2.eng: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of equanimity.
sn46.2:15.2.comm: This includes the development of absorption, which is the basis for the equanimity of the fourth absorption, as well as the development of insight into attraction and repulsion (see MN 152).

sn46.2:15.3.eng: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.2:15.4.pli: ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.
sn46.2:15.4.eng: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of equanimity, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.2:16.1.pli: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati;
sn46.2:16.1.eng: This body is sustained by food. It depends on food to continue, and without food it doesn’t continue.

sn46.2:16.2.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, ime satta bojjhaṅgā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhantī”ti.
sn46.2:16.2.eng: In the same way, the seven awakening factors are sustained by fuel. They depend on fuel to continue, and without fuel they don’t continue.”

sn46.20:1.1.pli: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti.
sn46.20:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, the seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

sn46.20:1.3.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.20:1.4.pli: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattantī”ti.
sn46.20:1.4.eng: These seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”

sn46.21:1.1.pli: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
sn46.21:1.1.eng: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and said to him:

sn46.21:2.2.eng: How are the awakening factors defined?”

sn46.21:2.3.pli: “‘Bodhāya saṃvattantī’ti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā bojjhaṅgāti vuccanti.
sn46.21:2.3.eng: “Mendicant, they’re called awakening factors because they lead to awakening.

sn46.21:2.4.eng: A mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.21:2.5.pli: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.
sn46.21:2.5.eng: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.21:2.6.eng: They’re called awakening factors because they lead to awakening.”

sn46.22:0.3.eng: A Teaching on the Awakening Factors

sn46.22:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you the seven awakening factors.

sn46.22:1.3.eng: And what are the seven awakening factors?

sn46.22:1.4.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.22:1.5.eng: These are the seven awakening factors.”

sn46.23:1.1.pli: “Kāmarāgaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati.
sn46.23:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, when you frequently apply the mind to things that are grounds for sensual greed, sensual desire arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.

sn46.23:1.2.pli: Byāpādaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati.
sn46.23:1.2.eng: When you frequently apply the mind to things that are grounds for ill will, ill will arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.

sn46.23:1.3.pli: Thinamiddhaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati.
sn46.23:1.3.eng: When you frequently apply the mind to things that are grounds for dullness and drowsiness, dullness and drowsiness arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.

sn46.23:1.4.pli: Uddhaccakukkuccaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati.
sn46.23:1.4.eng: When you frequently apply the mind to things that are grounds for restlessness and remorse, restlessness and remorse arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.

sn46.23:1.5.pli: Vicikicchāṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati.
sn46.23:1.5.eng: When you frequently apply the mind to things that are grounds for doubt, doubt arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.

sn46.23:2.1.pli: Satisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati …pe…
sn46.23:2.1.eng: When you frequently apply the mind to things that are grounds for the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of mindfulness arises, and once arisen it’s fully developed. …

sn46.23:2.2.pli: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti.
sn46.23:2.2.eng: When you frequently apply the mind to things that are grounds for the awakening factor of equanimity, the awakening factor of equanimity arises, and once arisen it’s fully developed.”

sn46.24:1.1.pli: “Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati;
sn46.24:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, when you apply the mind irrationally, sensual desire,

sn46.24:1.2.pli: anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati;

sn46.24:1.3.pli: anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati;

sn46.24:1.4.pli: anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati;

sn46.24:1.5.pli: anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati;
sn46.24:1.5.eng: and doubt arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.

sn46.24:1.6.pli: anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo nuppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo nirujjhati …pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo nuppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo nirujjhati.
sn46.24:1.6.eng: And the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity don’t arise, or if they’ve already arisen, they cease.

sn46.24:2.1.pli: Yoniso ca kho, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando nuppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando pahīyati;
sn46.24:2.1.eng: When you apply the mind rationally, sensual desire,

sn46.24:2.2.pli: anuppanno ceva byāpādo nuppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo pahīyati;

sn46.24:2.3.pli: anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṃ nuppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṃ pahīyati;

sn46.24:2.4.pli: anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṃ nuppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahīyati;

sn46.24:2.5.pli: anuppannā ceva vicikicchā nuppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā pahīyati.
sn46.24:2.5.eng: and doubt don’t arise, or if they’ve already arisen they’re given up.

sn46.24:3.1.pli: Anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati …pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti.
sn46.24:3.1.eng: And the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity arise, and once they’ve arisen, they’re fully developed.”

sn46.25:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you seven principles that prevent decline.
sn46.25:1.1.comm: Included along with several other “principles that prevent decline” at DN 16:1.8.11 and AN 7.26.

sn46.25:1.3.pli: Katame ca, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā?
sn46.25:1.3.eng: And what are the seven principles that prevent decline?

sn46.25:1.5.eng: They are the seven awakening factors.

sn46.25:1.7.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.25:1.8.pli: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā”ti.
sn46.25:1.8.eng: These are the seven principles that prevent decline.”

sn46.26:1.1.pli: “Yo, bhikkhave, maggo yā paṭipadā taṇhakkhayāya saṃvattati, taṃ maggaṃ taṃ paṭipadaṃ bhāvetha.
sn46.26:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, you should develop the path and the practice that leads to the ending of craving.

sn46.26:1.2.pli: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo katamā ca paṭipadā taṇhakkhayāya saṃvattati?
sn46.26:1.2.eng: And what is the path and the practice that leads to the ending of craving?

sn46.26:1.4.eng: It is the seven awakening factors.

sn46.26:1.6.eng: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.”

sn46.26:1.7.pli: Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
sn46.26:1.7.eng: When he said this, Udāyī said to him:

sn46.26:1.8.pli: “kathaṃ bhāvitā nu kho, bhante, satta bojjhaṅgā, kathaṃ bahulīkatā taṇhakkhayāya saṃvattantī”ti?
sn46.26:1.8.eng: “Sir, how are the seven awakening factors developed and cultivated so as to lead to the ending of craving?”

sn46.26:2.1.pli: “Idha, udāyi, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ.
sn46.26:2.1.eng: “Udāyī, it’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go. And it is abundant, expansive, limitless, and free of ill will.
sn46.26:2.1.comm: Here (and at SN 46.28:2.1) the terms beginning with “abundant” are added to the usual formula; they are more familiar from the divine meditations (SN 42.8:12.1).

sn46.26:2.2.pli: Tassa satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvayato vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ taṇhā pahīyati.
sn46.26:2.2.eng: As they do so, craving is given up.
sn46.26:2.2.comm: Here we find a succinct presentation of the three “rounds” of dependent origination: defilements, deeds, and results. See SN 12.38:1.2 and note for discussion.

sn46.26:2.3.eng: When craving is given up, deeds are given up.

sn46.26:2.4.eng: When deeds are given up, suffering is given up. …

sn46.26:2.5.pli: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ.
sn46.26:2.5.eng: A mendicant develops the awakening factor of equanimity, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go. And it is abundant, expansive, limitless, and free of ill will.

sn46.26:2.6.pli: Tassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvayato vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ taṇhā pahīyati
sn46.26:2.6.eng: As they do so, craving is given up.

sn46.26:2.7.eng: When craving is given up, deeds are given up.

sn46.26:2.8.eng: When deeds are given up, suffering is given up.

sn46.26:2.9.pli: Iti kho, udāyi, taṇhakkhayā kammakkhayo, kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo”ti.
sn46.26:2.9.eng: And so, Udāyī, when craving ends, deeds end; when deeds end suffering ends.”
